questions.question: BK-437 scope: what should this PR cover?

options.label: Tags + checker + routing (Recommended)
options.description: Add TREE-n tags to both files, extend check_formal_trace.py with a restatement source, and add it to docs-gate so Alloy- or Lean-only diffs run it. Running the solvers themselves in CI stays out of scope and gets its own backlog item. Size S, matching the item.

options.label: Also run Alloy/Lean in CI
options.description: The same, plus new CI jobs that run alloy_check.sh and lean_check.sh. This closes the 'neither check runs in CI' half too, but adds Docker/toolchain jobs against ADR-0032's 20-job cap. Grows to M.

options.label: Tags + checker only
options.description: No CI routing change. The check runs in lint and verify-formal only, so an edit confined to the .als or .lean files is never checked in CI (BK-333's failure class).

questions.question: Which tag syntax should the Alloy and Lean files use?

options.label: `-- @spec TREE-n` in both (Recommended)
options.description: Both languages already accept `--` line comments, and the files use them. One regex covers .dfy (`//`) and .als/.lean (`--`). The tag sits on the line above the predicate or theorem it restates, like Dafny's tag above an ensures.

options.label: Lean docstring tag
options.description: Alloy uses `-- @spec`, but Lean puts `@spec TREE-n` inside the `/-- ... -/` docstring of each theorem. The tag shows up in Lean hover docs, but the checker needs a second, multi-line parse for Lean.

questions.question: What should the checker enforce for the restatements?

options.label: Dangling + completeness (Recommended)
options.description: Fail on a tag citing an undeclared ID (F3 analogue), and fail when a TREE section of spec 051 has no tag in a restatement that covers spec 051. The checker holds a file→spec map. This catches a new or renumbered section that a restatement missed. It cannot catch a wrong restatement: tags cite, they don't prove.

options.label: Dangling tags only
options.description: Fail only when a tag cites an ID that no spec declares. Cheaper, but a new TREE-013 with no Alloy or Lean counterpart passes silently, and that is the drift BK-437 names.

questions.question: Should the check be a lint gate or advisory?

options.label: Blocking gate (Recommended)
options.description: Exit 1 on violation, like the existing F1–F3. The current state can be fully tagged, so no baseline is needed, and the ripple cost is a tag edit in the same PR as a spec 051 change.

options.label: Advisory report
options.description: Print the restatement matrix and gaps but exit 0. Nothing blocks, and drift is only seen if someone reads the output.

questions.question: The /pr mechanical gate calls for `hatch run fast`. Run it before opening the PR?

options.label: Skip, targeted set is enough (Recommended)
options.description: Already green: 115 tests in test_check_formal_trace + test_gen_gate_inventory, ruff and format, check_formal_trace, check_traces, gen_backlogid, changelog, gate inventory, docs-framework, the commit hook's full lint, and Alloy 30/30 plus the Lean build. The diff touches no src/. No CI runs on a PR into store-model-axioms, so #1131's retarget to master will be the first full run.

options.label: Run `hatch run fast`
options.description: Runs the members of `all` this diff can affect (scripts/fast_gate.py selects them). Slower, and it holds the one-suite-per-machine lock while it runs.

options.label: Run lint + docs-gate only
options.description: The no-code path: adds docs-gate's strict mkdocs build and link scan, which exercise the README and formal README edits. No pytest.
